paper.title_en: Residual Galactic binary foreground in LISA stochastic gravitational-wave background inference: source power concentration and spectral degeneracy
paper.abstract_en: Galactic compact binaries are expected to form a dominant foreground in the millihertz band of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). Residual power from injected sources that do not meet the adopted recovery criteria can bias stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) inference or increase its uncertainty. We use LISA Data Challenge 2A Sangria injections and the Erebor comparison table to construct a catalog residual spectrum between 0.4 and 6.0 mHz with orbit-averaged long-wavelength Michelson \(X\) source powers. The source power concentration in each frequency bin determines the excess kurtosis of a random-phase source sum; instrumental noise and fiducial SGWB power strongly reduce the resulting excess kurtosis in most bins. The residual spectrum also overlaps an isotropic power-law SGWB in the mean binned power. We use a fixed covariance obtained by summing independent Fourier-mode power variances. For a frequency-independent SGWB with fiducial amplitude \(Ω_0=10^{-11}\), marginalizing over the dimensionless residual-power factor \(β\) increases the \(Ω_0\) uncertainty by \(13.6\%\) when the residual power is distributed uniformly over the Fourier frequencies in each bin. The largest Gaussian prior standard deviation on \(β\) that limits this increase to \(10\%\) is \(0.0073\). More concentrated distributions of the residual power among Fourier frequencies reduce the increase, reflecting unresolved frequency structure. Omitting the fiducial residual with the covariance held fixed shifts the best-fitting \(Ω_0\) by \(119.5\) times the uncertainty obtained with \(β\) fixed. This projection of the residual spectrum onto the SGWB spectrum is not a posterior detection significance. The numerical values are conditional on the catalog-level scalar power model, fixed instrumental noise, and independent mode-power covariance.

decision.selection_reason_zh: 论文研究LISA随机引力波背景分析中的银河双星前景残余问题，属于脉冲星计时阵（PTA）相关领域，方法严谨，结果明确。
decision.title_zh: LISA随机引力波背景推断中的残余银河双星前景：源功率集中与频谱简并
decision.abstract_zh: 银河系致密双星预计将在激光干涉空间天线（LISA）的毫赫兹波段形成主导前景。来自未达到采用恢复标准的注入源的残余功率可能会使随机引力波背景（SGWB）推断产生偏差或增加其不确定性。我们使用LISA Data Challenge 2A Sangria注入和Erebor比较表来构建0.4至6.0 mHz之间的目录残余谱，采用轨道平均长波长迈克尔逊\(X\)源功率。每个频率区间中的源功率集中决定了随机相位源和的超额峰度；仪器噪声和基准SGWB功率强烈降低了大多数区间中的超额峰度。残余谱也在平均分档功率中与各向同性幂律SGWB重叠。我们使用通过求和独立傅里叶模式功率方差获得的固定协方差。对于基准振幅\(Ω_0=10^{-11}\)的频率无关SGWB，当残余功率在每个区间内的傅里叶频率上均匀分布时，对无量纲残余功率因子\(β\)进行边际化会使\(Ω_0\)不确定性增加\(13.6\%\)。将这一增长限制在\(10\%\)以内的最大高斯先验标准差为\(0.0073\)。残余功率在傅里叶频率间的更集中分布会减少增长，反映了未分辨的频率结构。省略基准残余并保持协方差固定，会使最佳拟合\(Ω_0\)偏移\(119.5\)倍于\(β\)固定时的不确定性。残余谱向SGWB谱的这种投影并非后验检测显著性。数值结果取决于目录级标量功率模型、固定仪器噪声和独立模式功率协方差。
